title: I Ranked 27 Stocks. These 3 Came Out on Top.
description: 13 made my buy list, but only one had everything I was looking for.
body_html:
Happy Thursday! And welcome to Mid Week Movers.

The winning stocks from this series have averaged 25.9% returns through 2026. And today, we are looking for our next winner.

This week I ranked 27, stocks submitted by YOU, from worst to first. You all have gotten really good at finding great stocks, because 13 of them made it to the “buy” list. That is unusual.

But of course… only 1 can be the winner, with the right combination of fundamentals, strength and price action that can lead to high performance results.

Lets get started!

Not a “Buy” - and

I don’t like saying a stock is a “sell”… because then it implies to sell and some would even go on to short the asset. Shorting stocks in a technical bull market, is not a good long term approach. Stocks whose price action is below the 200 day moving average, get an automatic “no” from me. You cannot hit all time highs, 52 week highs, or 52 day highs…quickly… when price action is trending below there.

Understandably, some of you know Pan American Silver, is a position of my own. So why rank it at the bottom of this list and hold it at the same time? Recall, we buy strength, not weakness. We got hot on silver again back around July. Silver has not put in a new low since that point, only higher highs and higher lows. I will not add to PAAS until, when and if, it gets back above $76, which I think it will. Silver is just ranging right now, and this is a longer term trade designed for after the S&P 500 peaks. The other 3 eliminated stocks have made new lows, PAAS has not.

This stock went up TOO much…

Most stocks in this list do not have this issue… but I quickly scan for any stocks that have essentially went parabolic. International Seaways, has had a consistent uptrend since October 2025. This does not provide us a very good specific entry point (SEPA) for an entry. Additionally, despite the stock going up, the strength of the trend, relative strength, has been declining in ascension, slightly, over the year.

To be clear: this does not mean “sell” or that I think it is going to imminently crash. This is just not a great stock for a fresh investment today. There is no reason to fight this upwards trend today.

Weakest Relative Strength -

We have 27 stocks remaining, and here, I am looking to eliminate the stocks with the weakest trends. Though anything is possible, the best performing stocks typically will have strong already developed uptrends. To measure this, I compare the asset’s relative strength to the S&P 500. Just because these 8 stocks were eliminated here, does not mean it can’t go up. It was simply weaker than the remaining stocks. These stocks have a relative strength score below 65. Some special notes for some of these:

  • Occidental Petroleum Corp, and ExxonMobil, , of these 8 stocks, I think have the highest % chance of going back into a stronger more developed bullish trend. Keep these on your watchlist.

    • OXY would be in a buy territory when and if it achieved ~$64

    • XOM would be in a buy territory when and if it achieved ~$170

  • Guardant Health, , is a “recession resistant” stock. Though it has pulled back the last 2 days, I find it likely it will resume a bull trend (its still in one today, we just do not buy weakness). I would target this one, when and if it re-achieved $183.

  • Tempus AI, is also showing extreme strength in it’s recovery. A price above $89 would convince me of a resumption of longer term bull trend.

Bad Fundamentals

To be clear, these 3 stocks were not terrible. But because I am seeking to eliminate stocks from the top spot, and we are following rules, Ampco-Pittsburg, Frontline and Hewlett Packard Enterprise are eliminated from the list. AND are both trending upwards, and honestly look great for a continuation. But I have to follow rules, and each of these stocks, experienced declines annually in Earnings Per Share. We always care that greedy shareholders are making more money.

Special shoutout to Frontline, which we called out back in February after it popped on the StockTok Summary, which is now up 84%. Again, I would not bet against it, but its just not an optimal buy today.

Subscribe now

Eliminations for random reasons…

Applied Materials,

AMAT had a healthy bounce off the 200 day moving average. But that is it. I strongly prefer stocks that have at least 2 bounces, if not more. Trend, fundamentals and strength are all there… but not much structurally to convince me this stock should be #1 in our list.

Ciena Corporation,

Similar to AMAT, this stock just again broke off of its highs. I think it is likely the trend will continue, but not before some more consolidation. I would want to see at least 1 bounce in price action, and for price to be above $475 to consider this stock for a longer term bullish trend.

Sanmina Corporation,

This stock meets most technical requirements. Good earnings, positive trend. But two warnings signals have arose on 18 June and 26 June. You see 2 strong sell off days, and the price action was very reactive. We have not had any high volume buying days, to confirm, or deny, that bulls have regained control of the stock. Yes, we have higher lows, but no clear breakouts. This one, we need to see a high volume breakout to consider a longer term trend upwards.

We’re down to 13 stocks and this is where it got difficult.

Every stock remaining has strong earnings, a positive trend, and strong relative strength against the S&P 500. I think you could build an “ETF” out of these 13 and have a strong group of stocks for the weeks and months ahead.

But I’m not looking for 13 good stocks. I’m looking for the best opportunity today.

So I went a step further. I reviewed the longer-term charts, looked for weaknesses that weren’t obvious at first glance, and separated the remaining 13 into C Tier, B Tier, and my Top 3.

Seven made my B Tier. Three made the final cut. And one stock had everything I was looking for.
